# Question: generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut is **`concentric_only`**: identify the largest
frame, keep only nested frames with exactly the same center, and compute fill
depth from that subset. It fits all three canonical demonstrations because all
three use concentric frames.

An exact disagreement input is emitted by the repaired generator with:

```text
seed = 20261011
sample_index = 97
grid_h = 12
grid_w = 15
n_frames = 3
asymmetry_force = true
```

The full grid and outputs are retained in
`repo/generators/97f17772dd96/counterexamples/concentric-only-offset-inner/counterexample.json`.
On that input, the intended output and `concentric_only` output differ at 23
cells.

I checked the intended output by applying the selected Racket rule through
`Catalog.apply`. Its executed rule hash is `1fab8c098fd0`, matching both the
catalog and the repaired generator's pin. The independent Python `rule_mirror`
matched Racket exactly, `self_check` passed, the exact requested axes were
observed, and the `offset_inner_frame` witness fired. The reproducible builder is
`repo/generators/97f17772dd96/workspace/build_counterexample.py`; its retained
execution output is `checks/counterexample-build.log`.

Yes, the proposed generator emits such cases in ordinary production. Offset
profiles are part of its ordered six-profile curriculum. The final semantic
census saw the witness in 401/600 draws, and the 300-lesson production census
refuted `concentric_only` in every lesson in every difficulty band. Required
hold-one-out query rotation also found 0 ambiguous rotations out of 1,200.
